title: Chapter 2
text: Big City Food Biographies Series Series Editor Ken Albala, University of the Pacific, kalbala@pacific.edu Food helps define the cultural identity of cities in much the same way as the distinctive architecture and famous personalities. Great cities have one-of-a-kind food cultures, offering the essence of the multitudes who have immigrated there and shaped foodways through time. The Big City Food Biographies series focuses on those metropolises celebrated as culinary destinations, with their iconic dishes, ethnic neighborhoods, markets, restaurants, and chefs. Guidebooks to cities abound, but these are real biographies that will satisfy readers’ desire to know the full food culture of a city. Each narrative volume, devoted to a different city, explains the history, the natural resources, and the people that make that city’s food culture unique. Each biography also looks at the markets, historic restaurants, signature dishes, and great cookbooks that are part of the city’s gastronomic make-up. Books in the Series New Orleans: A Food Biography , by Elizabeth M. Williams
